explanations.explanation: A donkey it is, friend. Jesus says they'll find one tied there, with her colt beside her (Matthew 21:2). He tells them to untie both and bring them to Him. Two animals, one errand, and the disciples get the whole plan before they even leave.
A camel would make for a tall errand, friend. But Jesus says they'll find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her (Matthew 21:2). I think a camel would've been a LOT to untie.

I get why a horse comes to mind, friend. A horse sounds like the ride for a big entrance. But Jesus says the two will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her (Matthew 21:2). The donkey matters later, too, so keep it in your pocket.

True, friend! Jesus says, “If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.” (Matthew 21:3) So the answer to the question is already in the disciples' pockets. Jesus hands them the whole script before they even leave.

It's actually True, friend. Jesus tells them, “If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.” (Matthew 21:3) The one who questions is the one who sends the animals. Easy to trip on, because those words are packed tight in one sentence.

Her King, friend! The prophet says, “See, your King comes to you…” (Matthew 21:5) The Daughter of Zion is Jerusalem's people, and the King is coming to HER. Not sending a letter, not calling ahead. Coming.

An army would be loud, friend, but that's not the word here. The prophet says, “See, your King comes to you…” (Matthew 21:5) The message to the Daughter of Zion is about a King. Not one soldier gets named.

A governor sounds official, friend, but the prophet uses a bigger word. He says, “See, your King comes to you…” (Matthew 21:5) The one coming to the Daughter of Zion is her King. Not a governor, not an army, a King.

Gentle, friend! The prophet says the King comes “…gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Matthew 21:5) Kings usually show up with a big loud entrance, so I think a gentle King on a donkey is a surprise. That's the word the text picks for Him.
I get it, friend. Kings usually bring a big scary entrance. But the prophet says this King comes “…gentle and riding on a donkey…” (Matthew 21:5) Gentle is the word the text gives.

Wealthy is a fair guess for a king, friend, but the prophet doesn't say it. He says the King comes “…gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.” (Matthew 21:5) Gentle is the word, and a donkey is the ride.

Not quite, friend. It's False. The text says they “…laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.” (Matthew 21:7) The cloaks go on the animals, and Jesus is sitting on them. That matches what the prophet said, a King riding on a donkey (Matthew 21:5).

False is right, friend! The disciples “…laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.” (Matthew 21:7) The cloaks go on the animals, and Jesus rides. That's just what the prophet said, a King riding on a donkey (Matthew 21:5).

Cloaks AND branches, friend! “A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.” (Matthew 21:8) Some spread cloaks, and others cut branches from the trees. Both of them end up on the road for Jesus.

That sounds fancy, friend, but it's not in the text. “A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.” (Matthew 21:8) Cloaks and cut branches, that's what covers the road. Flowers and fine linen don't get a mention.

Golden coins on the road, friend? That would stop traffic! But the text says, “A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.” (Matthew 21:8) Cloaks and branches, nothing shiny.
The Son of David, friend! The crowds shout, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9) Those in front of Him and those behind Him are shouting. That's the first line the text gives.
Good thinking on a famous name, friend, but that's not what they shout. The crowds say, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9) The Son of David is the title in the text.
Aaron is a big name, friend, but not the one in this crowd. They shout, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” (Matthew 21:9) David is the name on their lips, and they say it loud.
It's False, friend. The whole city is stirred, and they ask, “Who is this?” (Matthew 21:10) That's a question about who He is. The crowds give the answer in the next verse (Matthew 21:11).
False is right, friend! When Jesus enters, the whole city is stirred and asks, “Who is this?” (Matthew 21:10) That's a city asking about Him. The crowds reply in the next verse (Matthew 21:11).

explanations.answer: The prophet from Nazareth in Galilee
explanations.explanation: The prophet from Nazareth in Galilee, friend! The crowds reply, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” (Matthew 21:11) That's the answer they give the stirred city. A name, a title and a hometown, all in one breath.

explanations.answer: The teacher from Bethany in Judea
explanations.explanation: Close on the shape, friend, but the details are off. The crowds reply, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” (Matthew 21:11) They say prophet, and they say Nazareth. Bethany and Judea aren't in their answer.

explanations.answer: The rabbi from Capernaum by the sea
explanations.explanation: That's a lot of nice details, friend, but they're not the crowd's. They reply, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.” (Matthew 21:11) The title is prophet, and the hometown is Nazareth.
